verses.text: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest time, honour does not suit a fool.
Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, a curse that is not deserved does not land on anyone.
A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
Do not answer fools in the foolish way they speak, or you will be just like them.
Answer fools as their foolishness deserves, or they will think they are wise.
Sending a message by a fool is like cutting off your own feet or drinking poison.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is as useless as a crippled person's legs.
Giving honour to a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is like a thorn bush in the hand of a drunk.
Hiring a fool or anyone who happens to pass by is like an archer who shoots at everyone.
A fool who repeats his foolishness is like a dog that goes back to its vomit.
Do you see someone who thinks they are wise? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
A lazy person says, "There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion is in the streets!"
As a door turns on its hinges, a lazy person turns over in bed.
A lazy person buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to lift it back to his mouth.
A lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven people who give sensible answers.
Getting involved in someone else's argument is like grabbing a stray dog by the ears.
Like a madman shooting burning arrows and deadly weapons
is someone who tricks their neighbour and then says, "I was only joking!"
Without wood a fire goes out. Without gossip an argument dies down.
As charcoal keeps embers glowing and wood keeps a fire burning, a quarrelsome person keeps arguments going.
The words of a gossip are like tasty snacks. They go down deep inside a person.
Smooth words from an evil heart are like cheap silver paint on a clay pot.
Hateful people hide their hatred with their words, but in their hearts they plan to deceive.
Even if they speak kindly, do not believe them, because their hearts are full of seven kinds of evil.
Their hatred may be hidden by lies, but their evil will be exposed in front of everyone.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone will be crushed by it when it rolls back.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and flattering words bring ruin.
